title: The Starry Night, Van Gogh
subject: art
description: In **1889**, from the asylum at Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, **Vincent Van Gogh** painted *The Starry Night*. The sky swirls: art stops copying the real world and starts speaking an emotion.

hero.hook: From a room in an asylum, Van Gogh painted a sky that refuses to behave.

blocks.text: *The Starry Night* (**1889**) is the most famous painting by **Vincent Van Gogh**, an artist born in the [[Netherlands]]. Painted at the asylum of Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, it marks a turning point: you no longer paint only what you see. You paint what you feel.
A swirling sky, a cypress like a black flame, an invented village: the work opens the way to the expressive art of the 20th century.

In **May 1889**, after the [[Arles drama with Gauguin]] (the crisis that cost him part of his ear), Van Gogh had himself committed to **Saint-Paul-de-Mausole**, near Saint-Rémy. He was given a room to paint in. The night view was born behind the bars of his window.

blocks.caption: The Saint-Rémy asylum: a place of confinement, and of intense work

blocks.text: The canvas mixes observation and invention. You can make out the Alpilles hills and a tall **cypress**. But the village is not an exact copy. Van Gogh rebuilt the landscape to serve the emotion.

sections.title: Sculpting the sky with a brush

blocks.text: Technically, Van Gogh used **impasto**: the paint is thick, almost carved. Eleven stars turn like nebulae. The orange moon glows. The sky becomes the real character.

blocks.caption: The cypress links earth to sky like a dark flame

blocks.text: The great scrolls of the sky recall the energy of [[The Great Wave off Kanagawa]], the Japanese print Van Gogh admired. He turned that force into a cosmos.
That gesture announces [[Art as inner expression]]: the canvas tells us a mood, not a weather report.

Van Gogh painted nearly **900 pictures** in ten years, but died in **July 1890** at Auvers-sur-Oise, aged **37**, almost unknown. It was his sister-in-law, **Johanna van Gogh-Bonger**, who saved the work: exhibitions, sales, and the publication of his letters to his brother Theo.

*The Starry Night* changed hands several times for little money, before entering the **MoMA** in New York. The despised canvas became an icon. The [[Fauves]], painters of violent color in the early 20th century, would claim him as an ancestor.

sections.title: A cypress pointing to the infinite

blocks.text: The cypress ties the ground to the sky, a bridge between life on earth and whatever lies beyond. Van Gogh wrote that looking at the stars made him dream of death as a journey. Modern studies even suggest that the bright star near the cypress could be Venus, seen at dawn.

events.title: Death at Auvers
events.detail: The artist dies at 37, still overlooked.

blocks.text: *The Starry Night* turns suffering into a visual language. Van Gogh does not copy the night here: he invents an inner sky, and opens the door to modern expressive art.
